svg.title: Put R = j + 8. If twice macro radius (j + 7)L is below the fine period, coincident periodic displacements there are identical, so M(i, z) ≤1. Nonzero multiplicity implies dist(i, parent z) ≤R, by multiplying the coarse distance by L, bounding the embedded-base displacement by (j + 7)L, adding the at-most-L/2 parent offset, and applying the triangle inequality and integer rounding. Therefore P i M(i, z) ≤(2R + 1)4. Grouping the finite displacement/plaquette sums proves the port identity with actual multiplicities; the period condition is needed for the column bound, not that identity. The macro census used here has a period qualification, already included in the step hypotheses.
